record.paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
record.original_question: Let r,q >= 3, let V be the q-th Veronese ring in r variables, and let N_p be the usual syzygy vanishing property. If p <= 3q - 3, does V satisfy N_p?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix integers r, q ≥ 3. Let S = k[x_1,...,x_r] be a polynomial ring over a field k, and let V = ⊕_{d≥0} S_{qd} denote the q-th Veronese subring of S (equivalently, the homogeneous coordinate ring of the q-th Veronese embedding of P^{r-1}). View V as a graded module over the polynomial ring R generated in degree 1 by a basis of S_q (so V is a quotient of R by the ideal of Veronese relations).

Recall Green–Lazarsfeld's property N_p: a projectively normal graded algebra V (with minimal free R-resolution F_•) is said to satisfy N_p if F_0 = R, and for every 1 ≤ i ≤ p the i-th term F_i is generated in degree i+1, i.e. all syzygies up to homological degree p are linear.

Question: For every integer p with 1 ≤ p ≤ 3q − 3, does the q-th Veronese ring V in r variables satisfy property N_p?
artifact.status_search_result: This is the Ottaviani–Paoletti conjecture (1998). Ottaviani and Paoletti proved the bound is sharp (failure of N_{3q-2}) and verified the conjecture for r = 3 (all q) and for (r,q) = (4,3). Greco and Martino later established N_6 for the third Veronese embeddings (q = 3, all r), confirming the conjecture in that case. The general case for r ≥ 5 and q ≥ 4 remains open.

status_evidence.title: Syzygies of Veronese embeddings (Ottaviani–Paoletti)
status_evidence.snippet: Ottaviani-Paoletti proved that the Veronese embedding does not satisfy N_p for p ≥ 3d-2 and conjectured the converse; proved for n=2 and for n=d=3.

status_evidence.title: N_6 property for third Veronese embeddings
status_evidence.snippet: Third Veronese embeddings satisfy property N_6, settling the Ottaviani-Paoletti conjecture for q=3.
